newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN suspects Iraq still concealing weapons.
newsitem.headline: UN suspects Iraq still concealing weapons.

text.p: The United Nations said on Friday it believed Iraq may still be concealing limited but significant quantities of weapons of mass destruction.

In a major half-year report to the Security Council, the U.N. Special Commission in charge of Iraqi disarmament said it "continues to believe that limited, but highly significant quantitites (of weapons) may remain, as Iraq has not been able to account for a number of proscribed missiles and certain high quality chemical and biological warfare agents."

The report, prepared by commission chairman Rolf Ekeus, said that despite considerable progress in ridding Iraq of chemical, biological and ballistic missiles, Iraq had still not told the full story of its weapons programmes or handed over all its prohibited arms and related materials.
"The commission has therefore not yet reached the stage where it can state with confidence that everything that is proscribed to Iraq has been identified and disposed of," Ekeus said.

Ekeus said that Iraq's declarations on germ warfare and munitions production were difficult to accept. He said that Iraq was unable to provide "full accounting of biological weapons produced and destroyed unilaterally."

A clean bill of health is a key requirement by the Security Council before the embargo on Iraqi oil exports can be lifted entirely. Iraq has been under stringent sanctions since its troops invaded Kuwait in August 1990.
